• Describe any treatment prior to this claim (include treatment outside of Delta

available at www1.deltadentalins.com/dentists/administrative-forms.html.

patient delivered through telehealth services on the same basis and to the same

in-person diagnosis, consultation, or treatment. 
Delta Dental will accept claims for services delivered through teledentistry. When 
providing such services, you must comply with all requirements of the applicable 
state board of dentistry or equivalent body, and all applicable state and federal laws

Please submit the claim for your patient interaction using the appropriate evaluation

are considered inclusive in overall patient management and are not billable to the

➓At Delta Dental, we want to work with you to process your claims successfully. We’ve 
provided the following tips and suggestions for producing clear, complete claims to help 
move them more smoothly through our claims processing system — whether they are 
electronic or paper claims. We appreciate your continued support of our efforts to  
enhance and improve our service.
Tips for submitting Delta Dental Premier® and Delta Dental PPO™ paper claims
Use:
•  A laser printer with black ink
•  A 10 point font and all capital letters
•   Six-digit dates with no spaces, slashes or dashes (for example, 120310 for  
December 3, 2010)
•  Standard size paper (8.5 x 11 inch) for claims and written documentation
•  Fees with decimal points (for example, 100.00; not 100)
Avoid:
•   Free-form text — use the “Tooth number or letter” field to indicate quadrant or arch 
(UR or L, for example) and the “Remarks” box for necessary comments or notes
•  Stray marks in spaces that should be left blank
•  Ditto marks or arrows to indicate duplicate information
•  Slashed zeros and crossed sevens
•  Writing on top of lines or outside of boxes 
•  Using correction fluid or a highlighter pen 
•  More than one font style on a claim
•  Photocopied claims that are blurred or skewed

Claims Processing Tips
Here are a few additional ways to help us process your Delta Dental Premier and Delta 
Dental PPO claims. 
Claim forms: 
•   Use claim forms in formats acceptable to Delta Dental and submit complete and 
accurate claims for all services provided to Enrollees, whether they are covered Plan 
Services or not. Include the fee regularly charged by the Participating Provider for the 
service rendered.
•   Indicate a quantity (the number of x-rays, for example) in the field on the claim 
specifically for this purpose. If the claim does not have this field, please list each item 
on a separate line. 
•   Be sure to enter the name of the dental plan enrollee in the space provided at the top 
of the form and in the dual coverage section. (Usually, the enrollee is the person who 
has the dental plan through his/her employment. In dual coverage cases, there will 
usually be two different enrollees within a family.)
•   Be sure to enter the treating dentist’s license number or National Provider Identifier 
(NPI). If you enter two NPIs (one for the treating dentist and another for the billing 
entity), please verify that they are both valid. 
Required provider information:
•  Tax Identifier number (TIN).
•  Treating provider license or National Provider Identifier (NPI).
•  Treating location.
•  Treating provider name.
Dual coverage:
•   Indicate if the patient has (or does not have) dual coverage with another dental plan 
(or sometimes, in oral surgery cases for example, with a medical plan) by checking the 
specific box, usually titled “Is patient covered by another plan of benefits?” or something 
similar. If there is dual coverage, be sure to include all the requested information.
•   Always include the primary carrier’s Explanation of Benefits or remittance advice 
document when Delta Dental is the secondary carrier.
Orthodontic claims: Please don’t send claims for monthly orthodontic visits. To make it 
easier for you, your fees for these visits are included in the total fee you submit on the 
claim for banding or orthodontic appliance insertion, and in the periodic payments you 
automatically receive from Delta Dental. 
Pre-treatment estimates: Send a new claim for payment after services are provided (do 
not date and return the pre-treatment estimate). In the “Remarks” section, include the 
Delta Dental reference number found on the original pre-treatment estimate, or write 
“Pre-treatment estimate on file” if you no longer have the reference number. 
Documentation:
•  See Section 4, Policies and Procedures, for documentation requirements to determine  
    which codes require you to submit imaging, charting and narratives.

CLAIM SUBMISSION GUIDELINESPage 5 – 9Tips To Help Us Process Your Claims (continued)
•   X-ray copies submitted with paper claims must be of diagnostic quality. We will accept 
duplicate films and paper copies of digital images. 
•   We do not return x-rays or other documentation submitted with paper claims; however, 
we will make an exception when we receive a stamped, self-addressed envelope with the 
claim. 
Avoid Late Claim Submission
When you submit claims as soon as possible after treatment is completed, you help us 
process claims more efficiently, using the patient’s most current eligibility and benefits to 
determine payment.
Dental claims will be processed in the order received. The first claim received, irrespective 
of the date of service, will be the first claim processed. Once paid, claims cannot be 
reprocessed to adjust the order of receipt.
Generally, claims received more than 12 months after the date of treatment may not be 
paid. However, some programs may require you to submit claims within a shorter period 
of time (e.g., 90 days for Texas CHIP program). To be sure, please refer to the dentist 
handbook specific to that program. If you receive notification that no payment was made 
because of late submission:
• The patient is responsible for his or her coinsurance/copayment portion only. The amount 
that would have been payable by Delta Dental may not be charged to the patient.
• If late submission occurred because of extenuating circumstances (for example, the 
patient did not advise you sooner of the existence of coverage), you may request a 
review of the decision to deny payment by submitting a claim adjustment. Please call or 
write to our Contact Center (and be sure to include all relevant information).
We recommend that you submit all your claims and attachments electronically for the most 
efficient processing.
Claim Adjustment Requests
Delta Dental requires that providers file a “claim adjustment” to resubmit claims for clerical 
corrections, or to provide additional information to support the original claim submitted. 
The claim adjustment request can now be submitted online (deltadentalins.com) by 
logging into your Provider Tools account and selecting My Claims. Find and select the claim 
you would like reviewed and include additional information to help support reprocessing of 
your claim:
• Include your reason for requesting a claim adjustment
• Attach copies of x-rays, photographs, and/or additional clinical comments
Claim adjustment requests are processed within 30 days. You can track the status from 
beginning to end on your dispute dashboard. A Provider Dispute can be initiated for a 
claim once the provider has made an initial effort to resubmit the claim for an adjustment 
before initiating the dispute process. Provider Disputes can also be filed online. Generally, 
Delta Dental allows one claim adjustment per claim.

QUALITY MANAGEMENTPage 6 – 1Quality Program Overview 
Delta Dental is committed to ensuring enrollees have access to quality dental services 
in a safe setting, which it manages through its Quality Program. Delta Dental’s Quality 
Program (QP) is established according to the guidelines set forth by the Centers for 
Disease Control and the American Dental Association. 
The Quality Program is the cornerstone of Delta Dental’s commitment to its enrollees 
and contracted network. Delta Dental is responsible for exercising oversight of the 
quality of care and quality of service that is provided by the dentist contracting with the 
network. 
This Section describes the QP’s policies, procedures, standards, and guidelines. When 
material changes are made to the QP, this Section will be updated.
Peer Review Committee
Delta Dental’s Peer Review Committee (PRC), comprised of dentists and specialists 
in good standing, reviews cases in which a potential deficiency of quality of care, 
professional ethics, access, availability, and/or quality of service has been identified.  
Deficiencies are identified through ongoing quality monitoring activities of Delta Dental.
The PRC evaluates and discusses cases with identified deficiencies that meet or exceed 
established thresholds and recommends the assignment of a Corrective Action Plan 
(CAP) to the offending provider and/or facility, when appropriate. In most cases, 
providers and facilities will be given the opportunity to correct any deficient areas. 
However, when a deficiency finding puts enrollees at risk of imminent danger or falls 
below standards of care to an extent that creates a known risk to patient safety, as 
defined solely by the Delta Dental Peer Review Committee, Delta Dental may take 
immediate action to suppress a member dentist in a network, suspend or terminate a 
provider’s participation in a network, report to governing bodies, or take other action as 
deemed necessary by Delta Dental to protect enrollees.
Quality Assessment Review (QAR)
Delta Dental Member Dentists and facilities are reviewed periodically to ensure they 
are meeting the standards of care and Delta Dental criteria. QARs can be triggered for 
a variety of reasons, including but not limited to random selection or as the result of a 
grievance reported to Delta Dental.
We will contact you to schedule the QAR and work with you to minimize impacts to 
your business. Your Dental Consultant will answer any questions you have regarding 
your QAR at the time of scheduling to help prepare you and your office. We recommend 
reviewing the Quality Assessment Review Criteria listed below in detail prior to your 
audit as it explains all requirements and evaluation criteria for you. 
At the conclusion of the QAR, the Consultant will provide you with the results of 
the review. After the completion of a review by Delta Dental, a QAR Results Letter 
will be sent to the member dentist/facility. This letter will again provide the results 
of the review including any areas identified for improvement. Please read these 
results carefully and follow any requested next steps. If there are deficient findings 
during a review based on compliance with this Delta Dental Dentist Handbook or the 
Participating Provider Agreement, then a Potential Quality Issue (PQI) score will be 
assigned for appropriate follow up by Delta Dental. 
If there are deficient findings during a QAR that warrant a concern for patient safety 
or that are suspected to deviate from expected provider performance, clinical care, 
or outcome of care, then a Potential Quality Issue (PQI) score will be assigned for Quality Management

QUALITY MANAGEMENTPage 6 – 2appropriate follow up from Delta Dental. PQI scores of 1 can be remedied by the 
provider with a correction of any outstanding findings as outlined in the QAR Results 
Letter and attachments. PQI scores of 2 and 3 require review by Delta Dental’s Peer 
Review Committee for potential assignment of a Corrective Action Plan to the offending 
provider/facility. Corrective Action Plans typically include assignment of Continuing 
Education courses in applicable areas and remedy of the deficiency within an assigned 
time period for the provider/facility to remain a member in good standing. In most cases, 
member dentists and facilities will be given the opportunity to correct any deficient 
areas. However, when a deficiency finding puts enrollees at risk of imminent danger or 
falls below standards of care to an extent that creates a known risk to patient safety, 
as defined solely by the Delta Dental Peer Review Committee, Delta Dental may take 
immediate action to suppress a member dentist in the network, suspend or terminate a 
provider’s participation in a network, or take other action as deemed necessary by Delta 
Dental to protect enrollees.
A quality assessment typically takes two to three hours. It includes a facility structure 
review and a patient chart review. The structure review focuses on the contracted 
provider’s dental office, its staff, its equipment, and the office environment. A chart 
review focuses of the completeness and adequacy of dental records, quality of care, and 
outcomes. 
The following criteria are always expected and required for a member dentist and/or 
member facility to receive a “satisfactory” rating during a review.
Facility Structure Criteria 
1) Provider Standards for Appointment Access – Delta Dental Premier and PPO Plans
  Dental offices of every Delta Dental participating dentist are required to meet the 
following access and appointment availability standards:
 a.  Emergency care shall be available 24 hours a day, 7 days per week. An active 
after-hours mechanism, including but not limited to an answering machine, 
answering service, a monitored cell phone, or a pager, must be active and 
available to all enrollees 24 hours per day, 7 days per week and must provide 
enrollees with information about how they may obtain urgent or emergency 
care including, when applicable, how to contact another provider who has 
agreed to be on-call to triage or screen by phone or, if needed, deliver urgent or 
emergency care.
 b.  In accordance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, urgent care shall 
be provided within 72 hours from the initial diagnosis, or less, depending on the 
individual needs of the patient and the generally accepted standards of dentistry.
 c.  Non-urgent initial visits, or visits for routine care shall be available within 36 
business days of the enrollee’s request.
 d.  Preventative dental care appointments, such as hygiene appointments, shall be  
available within 40 business days of the enrollee’s request.
 e.  Facilities must meet current Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) access 
guidelines, including wheel-chair accessibility.
 f.  Patients requiring Language Assistance must have access to such assistance. 
Please refer to the Language Assistance Program section (2-9) of this manual for 
details on how to obtain language assistance for Delta Dental enrollees needing 
interpretation and/or translation services. (California specific requirement)
*State regulations may vary by stateQuality Assessment Review Criteria

QUALITY MANAGEMENTPage 6 – 32) Recall, Failed or Cancelled Appointments
 a.  Dental offices shall have an effective system for following-up on cancelled, 
broken and missed appointments in place which ensures timely rescheduling 
of a new appointment in a manner which is appropriate for the patient’s health 
care needs, and which ensures continuity of care consistent with generally 
accepted standards of dentistry and all applicable laws, rules and regulations.
 b.  All patients shall be placed on a recall system, which is office-initiated and 
proactive in nature, such as the sending of “reminder” postcards, making 
telephone calls to the patient or scheduling recall appointments in advance.
 c.  The next recommended recall appointment shall be documented in the patient’s 
chart record.
3) Facility and Equipment Standards
 a.  Dental office facilities and equipment must be clean, safe, well-maintained and 
in good repair in accordance with the generally accepted practices of dentistry 
and all applicable laws rules and regulations.
 b.  Dental office facilities must be in compliance with current mercury hygiene 
practices and all state and federal mercury handling regulations.
 c.  Nitrous oxide equipment must be clean, safe and in good repair in accordance 
with the generally accepted practices of dentistry and all applicable laws rules 
and regulations.
  d.  The nitrous oxide equipment must have a nitrous oxide recovery or exhaust 
system in place and operational.
 e.  The nitrous oxide equipment must have in place a failsafe mechanism to ensure 
the correct volume and ratio of oxygen.
 f.  A lead apron and thyroid collar, whether separate or attached, must be present 
and must be used on all patients receiving radiographs.
 4) Emergency Procedures and Equipment
 a.  Dental office facilities must have current written emergency protocols for fire 
and other natural disasters, which includes a plan indicating escape routes, staff 
member responsibilities, and a call directory for emergency services.
 b. Exits must be clearly marked with exit signs.
 c.  Emergency telephone numbers must be posted in a clearly visible place 
accessible to all employees, patients and visitors. This directory must include 
(but is not limited to) 911, poison control and the local 7-digit numbers for Fire 
and Ambulance services.
 d.  A medical emergency kit must be available on-site. The medical emergency 
kit must be readily available, easily accessible, and labeled with an inventory 
of its contents. The drugs and contents of the emergency kit must conform 
to generally accepted standards as determined by the ADA and state dental 
boards. Staff must be aware of the location of the emergency kit and must be 
trained in the general use of the emergency kit.
 e.  A portable oxygen supply tank with a face mask or an Ambu Bag must be 
available. Oxygen tank delegated for emergency medical use must have no Quality Assessment Review Criteria (continued)

QUALITY MANAGEMENTPage 6 – 4less than 25% volume. Staff must be aware of and have access to the portable 
oxygen supply and must be trained in the use of the portable oxygen supply.
5) Sterilization and Infection Control
 a.   Sterilization and infection control standards must conform to the current CDC, 
and OSHA Guidance. 
 b. Protocols for sterilization procedures must be posted per state guidelines. 
 c.  All sterilizers in the designated sterilization area, whether in current use or not, 
will be monitored weekly using biological (spore) testing. Sterilizers not being 
used must be removed from the designated sterilization area.
 d.  All contaminated instruments and handpieces will be properly cleaned, 
sterilized, and stored in accordance with all applicable laws, rules, and 
regulations. Handpieces and instruments will be sterilized between patients and 
bagged until used.
 e.  Staff must wear utility gloves while cleaning contaminated instruments.
 f.  Ultrasonic cleaning solutions must be changed per the manufacturer’s 
recommendations.
 g.  If a cold high-level sterilization solution is used, a log must be kept monitoring 
the changing of the sterilization solution in accordance with the manufacturer’s 
recommendations. The log must document the date of expiration of the fresh 
solution and the dates the solution was changed. (In California, the name of the 
staff member who changed the high-level sterilization fluid must appear in the 
log).
 h.  High level sterilization solutions must be used only on instruments that cannot 
be subjected to other methods of sterilization. The cold sterilization (high-level 
disinfectant) must be an EPA registered brand of tuberculocidal, hospital-grade 
disinfectant.
 i.  Instruments which cannot be autoclaved or cold-sterilized must be disposable 
and must be disposed of immediately after use.
 j.  Staff and the dentist must wear appropriate personal protective equipment. 
Personnel shall always use protective gloves, masks, eyewear, coats, or gowns 
during patient care. Splattered masks and garments must be replaced as 
necessary and must be replaced between patients. Gloves must be changed 
between patients and before leaving the operatory.
 k.  Appropriate and adequate barrier techniques must be used in dental treatment 
areas. All operatory hard surfaces must be disinfected between patients and at 
the end of each day. An OSHA/EPA-approved solution must be used. Surfaces 
not capable of being disinfected by routine methods must be covered with 
impervious materials.
 l.  Handpieces and waterlines must be flushed, as dictated by ADA, CDC and state 
infection control guidelines between patients and at the beginning of each day 
of patient treatment.
 m.  Infection control and cross-contamination prevention procedures must be 
followed for instruments, materials, impressions, and dental devices transferred 
between the dental office and in-house or external dental laboratories. 
Impressions, dentures, and other appliances, such as crowns, bridges, and Quality Assessment Review Criteria (continued)

dental laboratories. In the dental laboratory, the pumice pan must be changed

Patient Chart Criteria 
1) Documentation
 A. Medical History
  1. Comprehensive Information Collection
   a.  Each patient’s medical history must record information pertaining to 
their general health and appearance, presence of any systemic disease 
or underlying conditions including whether they are being managed by a 
healthcare provider, allergies and reactions to anesthetics.
   b.  The medical history must record all current medication(s) and medical   
treatment(s). A proactive (“Yes” — “No”) format is recommended, as long 
as the answer is “yes” the patient is asked for more specific information 
such as the type and dosage of medication(s) they are taking, etc.
   c.  The medical history must record the name and telephone number of the 
patient’s current primary care or treating physician, and the name and 
telephone number of the person to contact in case of an emergency.
   d.  The patient (or in the case of a child, the parent,) must sign and date all 
initial medical histories.
  2. Medical Follow-Up
   a.  Patient comments, dentist’s notes, and comments regarding consultations 
with physicians must be documented in the patient’s chart.
  3. Appropriate Medical Alert
   a.  Medical alerts (diabetes, high blood pressure, heart conditions, etc.) must 
be uniform and conspicuously located on the portion of the patient chart 
used during treatment and must reflect current medical history.
  4. Dentist Signature and Date
   a.  Dentists must sign and date all initial histories after reviewing with the 
patient.
  5. Periodic Update
   a.  Documentation of medical history updates must occur in the patient 
chart at least annually or more frequently when there is a change to the 
medical history. Medical history updates must be signed by the patient 
and the dentist. Medical history updates are acceptable on the medical 
history form or in the progress notes and must reflect whether there are 
changes or no changes. Recommended frequency for medical history 
updates is annually unless the patient indicates there has been a change 
in medical status.
 B. Dental History — Chief Complaint
  1.  Documentation of the patient’s chief complaint at each visit and pertinent 
information relative to the patient’s dental history must appear in the 
patient’s dental record.Quality Assessment Review Criteria (continued)

  1. Status of Teeth and Existing Conditions
   a.  The patient’s dental record must contain a grid or narrative to document               
existing restorations and conditions.
  2. TMJ and Occlusal Evaluation
   a.  The patient’s dental record must include evidence of a TMJ exam and an 
evaluation of occlusion (classification).
  3. Prosthetics
   a.  The patient’s dental record must include an evaluation of existing 
appliances, including the age and condition of the appliances, the teeth

  4. Status of Periodontal Condition
   a.  The patient’s dental record must document the periodontal condition 
of gingival tissues, the presence and degree of calculus, the presence 
and degree of plaque, and the presence and degree of bleeding on 
periodontal probing.
   b.  The patient’s dental record must contain baseline periodontal pocket     
probing measurements.
   c.  The dental record must document the periodontal case type or 
classification: (Case Type I-V) or (Normal, Gingivitis, Early Periodontitis, 
Moderate Periodontitis, Severe Periodontitis).
  5. Soft Tissue — Oral Cancer Exam
   a.  The patient’s dental records must include documentation of a soft tissue 
and oral cancer exam. The soft tissue and oral cancer exam must be 
performed and documented at the initial visit and then performed and 
documented periodically, at least annually.
   b. Treatment records must note any anatomical abnormalities.
 D. Progress Notes 
  1. Progress notes must be detailed and, if handwritten, legible and in ink. 
   a.  Corrections to progress notes should be made in such a way as to 
see what was previously noted and what the corrected information is.

 A. Radiographs
  1. Quantity and Frequency
   a.  There must be an adequate number of radiographs to make an 
appropriate diagnosis and treatment plan and at regular, periodic 
intervals, in accordance with current ADA and FDA recommendations. 
   b.  Whenever possible, radiographs must not be taken if recent, acceptable, 
films are available from another source, such as from a previous dentist.

   a.  Radiographs must not have overlapping contacts. Radiographs must not 
have cone cuts that affect diagnostic value. Periapical radiographs must 
completely demonstrate root apices.
   b.  Radiographs must be of diagnostic quality, have good contrast, and must 
not be over or underdeveloped.
  3.  Mounted, Labeled and Dated 
   a.  All radiographs not in electronic format must be mounted, labeled and

   b.  Digital radiographs must be arranged, labeled, time-stamped, and dated 
and include all images taken of the patient.
  4. Electronic Radiographs 
   a.  Digital radiographs must be evaluated and stored in an un-filtered and

 B. Treatment Plan 
  1.  Written or typed treatment plans must be present in all patient charts. If the

includes or consists of a fillable form and/or checklist, it must be completed 
in ink. 
   a.  Treatment plans must be comprehensive and must document patient 
needs and treatment recommendations.
   b.  Alternative treatment plans must be documented and must clearly 
indicate the treatment option(s) (including the choice of no treatment) 
that the patient has reviewed, elected and/or declined to have performed.
   c.  Consultations and referrals must be noted in the treatment record, 
including the name and contact information of the provider the 
consultation or referral is being sent to. The patient must also be provided 
with this information.

  1.  Proposed treatment must be sequenced in order of clinical need and must 
be consistent with diagnostic and examination findings, and in compliance 
with generally recognized and accepted professional standards. A sample 
treatment sequence is as follows:
   a. Relief of pain, discomfort and infection;
   b. Prophylaxis and instructions for preventive care;
   c.  Treatment of extensive caries and pulpal inflammation; endodontic 
therapy;
   d. Periodontal treatment;
   e. Restorative treatment and replacement of missing teeth;
   f.  Placement of the patient on a recall schedule with documentation of the 
recall schedule in the progress notes.Quality Assessment Review Criteria (continued)

Delta Dental’s Utilization Management (UM) program includes the following           
elements:
• Benefit limitations and exclusions based on the enrollee’s plan design
•  Delta Dental Processing Policies and Procedures (which reflect clinical 
evaluation guidelines)
• Procedure based reviews by a dental consultant
• Focused review of specific dentists
• Analytic systems to identify aberrant utilization of dental procedures
• Professional review of selected dental claims based on systematic analysis of 
procedure and utilization patterns
 Delta Dental’s UM program analyzes and evaluates the utilization of services to 
ensure that treatment is necessary and appropriate; claims submission complies 
with our billing, documentation and benefit guidelines; and identify those dentists 
who provide services outside the community standard of care. Consideration is 
given to individual patient needs and clinical circumstances. UM decision making is 
based only on appropriateness of care and service and existence of coverage.  
Delta   Dental does not reward its dental consultants or other individuals for issuing 
denials of coverage or care. There are no financial incentives for dental consultants 
or other UM staff to encourage decisions that result in underutilization.
The Utilization Committee establishes the UM program policies and procedures 
and oversees retrospective reviews. The Utilization Committee is made up of 
senior dental professionals, data analysts and managerial staff within Delta Dental.  
The Utilization Committee reports to the appropriate governing bodies (or their 
delegated subcommittees) of Delta Dental of California, Delta Dental Insurance 
Company, Delta Dental of Pennsylvania and affiliated companies.
The Utilization Committee’s responsibilities include:
• Developing and refining UM program policies and procedures, including 
clinical criteria
• Establishing thresholds for peer-to-peer comparison of utilization levels
• Establishing dentist corrective action and/or sanctions for non-compliance 
with the UM program
• Conducting retrospective review of utilization data and dentist practice 
patterns
• Determining contracting dentist compliance with UM program policies and 
procedures and overseeing corrective actions and/or sanctions for non- 
compliance
• Reviewing the UM program on an annual basis and making recommendations 
for revisions to the program as needed
2) Focused Review
Delta Dental has established the Focused Review process to help monitor claims 
and ensure accurate processing and contract compliance. Dentists may be selected 
for Focused Review based upon a claims analysis showing a statistical difference 
from their peers, patient complaints or on a random basis. Dentists who are placed Utilization Management Program

QUALITY MANAGEMENTPage 6 – 14on Focused Review will need to submit additional documentation beyond what 
is normally required for processing claims and pre-treatment estimates. Dentists 
selected for Focused Review will receive information on the procedure codes that 
will require additional documentation and how to submit these claims for Focused 
Review.
 Following an analysis of all reports and data to identify dentists with indicators 
of over or under-utilization of services and/or practice patterns inconsistent with  
normative data, a report summarizing the results is prepared for presentation to 
the Utilization Committee. The Utilization Committee evaluates the case report and 
determines whether aberrant practice patterns are a result of practice demographics 
or other explainable conditions for a dentist and whether patient activity was 
unusual, but appropriate for the particular situation. Results that do not appear to 
have a justifiable basis for deviation from norms are recommended for further review 
and may result in a recommendation to place the dentist on Focused Review.
When a dentist is placed on Focused Review, they will be asked to submit additional 
documentation for a defined period for pertinent procedures. In addition, dentists 
may also be asked to submit additional documentation for specific claims on a 
case-by-case basis. The additional documentation will be used to adjudicate each 
of these claims or pre-treatment estimates. Delta Dental will also analyze the claims 
submitted during the Focused Review period and consider whether to remove the 
dentist from Focused Review.  A dentist may be removed from Focused Review after 
the Utilization Committee determines that billed services were generally necessary 
and appropriate, and complied with our billing, documentation, and benefit 
guidelines. If additional information is needed beyond the initial Focused Review 
period, the Focused Review status may continue on a month-to-month basis.
If a dentist is placed on Focused Review, they will receive a letter explaining the 
process. It is very important to read through the information, which will ensure a 
smooth process.

In addition to procedural review and focused review, individual claims and

These criteria include rules that are based on procedure and utilization patterns. 
As with all claims and pre-treatment estimates, the documents that are selected

Any procedures may be selected for Professional Review; even procedures that do

Patient Record Expectations:
The recording of accurate patient information is essential to dentistry. The dental 
record, also referred to as the patient chart, is the official collection of documents 
that contains all diagnostic information, imaging, clinical notes, treatment(s) 
performed, laboratory slips/invoices, and patient-related communication(s) that 
occur in the dental office, including instructions for home care, consent to treatment 
and treatment estimates, etc. If a document or image includes a patient’s name, it 
is considered part of their record. Complete and accurate records should contain 
enough information to allow any other provider (who has no prior knowledge of the 
patient) to understand the patient’s treatment history and to continue that patient’s 
care based on that record. The patient record, whether paper or electronic, should 
be consistent with the patient’s medical history and accurately reflect their oral 
condition on each date of service. 
Complete and Accurate also means that patient records are created at the time of 
service. Patient notes, chart updates, entries into office software, etc. which are not 
entered on the same date as the services rendered do not constitute a complete 
and accurate record. Delta Dental does not accept the addition of treatment notes 
after the date of a request for patient records or after receipt of findings in an 
investigation indicating that the services billed on a claim are not notated in the 
patient record. The patient’s record must be complete before a claim is submitted 
for services. All Attending Dentist’s Statements and the patient treatment record 
shall accurately identify the rendering/treating provider (individual(s) who physically 
performed the services), the office location where the services were performed, 
and all of the services completed and/or delivered on that date. Failure to bill the 
correct rendering/treating provider, service location, and/or services performed 
on an Attending Dentist Statement may be considered fraudulent and subject 
to recoupment of claim payment, termination from the network, referral to law 
enforcement, and/or all of the other corrective and disciplinary actions noted above.
For further guidance on Delta Dental’s requirements for documentation and patient 
records, see the Processing Policies and Procedures (Section 4) and the Quality 
Management (Section 6) sections.
Participating Provider(s) shall not bill for services that they perform on themselves or 
for services rendered to them by their dental support staff.

Providers, both contracted and non-contracted, may file a dispute of a claim that

substantially similar billing or contractual disputes that are individually numbered.
Delta Dental requires that providers file a “claim adjustment” to resubmit claims 
for clerical corrections, or to provide additional information to support the original 
claim submitted. The claim adjustment request can now be submitted online 
(deltadentalins.com) by logging into your Provider Tools account and selecting My 
Claims. Find and select the claim you would like reviewed and include additional 
information to help support reprocessing of your claim. Claim adjustment requests 
are processed within 30 days. You can track the status from beginning to end on your 
dispute dashboard. A Provider Dispute may be filed for a claim denied for reasons 
other than those described above, or to dispute a claims adjustment decision.

For providers in California, Delta Dental’s Provider Dispute Resolution process 
is based on the provisions of Section 1300.71.38 of Title 28, California Code of 
Regulations. Delta Dental processes provider grievances in accordance with these 
guidelines. The dispute process for providers in Maryland is governed by and subject 
to Maryland laws and regulations.
Procedure:
The provider must submit a written dispute to Delta Dental within 365 days of the 
action precipitating the dispute, or in the case of inaction, within 365 days of the 
expiration date for contesting or denying the claim.
If the disputed issue involves a claim, the following information must be included in 
the provider’s dispute:
• The provider’s name
• Provider’s state license number and taxpayer identification number (TIN)
• Provider’s contact information
• The claim number
• A clear description of the disputed matter
• The date of service
• A clear explanation of why the provider believes Delta Dental’s action was 
incorrect

www1.deltadentalins.com/dentists/administrative-forms.html, to submit their appeals 
to help ensure all required information is submitted.

• A clear explanation of the issue and the provider’s position.
• If the dispute involves a patient or group of patients, a clear explanation of the 
disputed issue, including the date(s) of service and the provider’s position.
Provider disputes are tracked from the time they are received at Delta Dental to the 
time the dispute is resolved and closed. Each dispute is assigned a unique tracking

engaged in behavior for which CMS could have revoked the individual or entity to the 
extent applicable if they had been enrolled in Medicare and CMS determines that the

Medicare program.

can no longer be made to the precluded provider and allow the enrollee 60 days to find 
another treating dentist before claim payment denials will begin.

List, the provider will no longer be eligible for payment from the Plan and is prohibited 
from pursuing payment from the beneficiary. The provider will hold financial liability 
for services, items and drugs that are furnished, ordered, or prescribed after this 60-
day period, at which point both the provider and enrollee will have already received 
notification of the provider’s preclusion.

participating dentist of the amount payable by the Enrollee at or before the time of 
making payment to the dentist of Delta Dental’s obligation for Plan Services. The 
dentist shall be bound by Delta Dental’s determination of the amount payable by the 
Enrollee, unless he/she notifies Delta Dental in writing of his/her disagreement with such 
determination pursuant to Section 12 of these Rules. The dentist shall not charge the 
Enrollee for the amount in disagreement until the dispute is resolved.

for, any amount payable by Delta Dental under the terms of the Enrollee’s Plan, whether 
or not payment is made by Delta Dental.

these Rules, it shall take appropriate action, including but not limited to recouping the

Attending Dentist’s Statement for services performed in a dental practice or facility 
in which another dentist having an interest in the dental practice or facility, such as 
an owner, partner, shareholder or manager, is any of the following: (a) a participating 
dentist who is subject to mandatory prior authorization; or (b) a participating dentist

participating dentist practices. Assignment of amounts due from Delta Dental to any

grounds for terminating the participating dentist agreement.

(personal injury and property) insurance on the dentist’s office premises, in at least the

dentist shall notify Delta Dental immediately of any insurance coverage cancellation 
or other failure to maintain any credentialing requirement. A participating dentist shall 
notify Delta Dental of any language assistance capability of the participating dentist or 
the office staff, and any changes in such capability. A participating dentist must contact 
Delta Dental if an Enrollee requests or evidently requires interpretation services in any 
language, and Delta Dental will immediately arrange for such services at no cost to the 
enrollee or the participating dentist.

Section 1. Name. 
The name of this corporation shall be DELTA DENTAL OF CALIFORNIA.
Section 2. Nonprofit. 
This corporation is organized pursuant to the General Nonprofit Corporation Law, and shall 
conduct its affairs and business without pecuniary gain or other profit to its members and 
without distribution of any gain or dividends to its members; provided that members may 
receive compensation for professional services rendered and for services given as an officer or 
other employee of the corporation.

the spouse of a dentist and does not have a significant financial interest in any entity or 
organization which provides dental or other health care services to this corporation.

As used in these Bylaws, “Holding Company” shall mean the nonprofit entity established 
pursuant to the February 17, 2000 resolution of the Board of Directors of this corporation. 
The members of the Executive Committee of this corporation selected pursuant to Article 
V, Section 6(f) of these Bylaws shall serve as directors of the Holding Company and shall 
collectively be entitled to cast at least 55% of all votes that may be cast by all Holding 
Company directors.Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

APPENDIX A - California Provider DocumentsPage A – 8ARTICLE II — MEMBERSHIP
Section 1. Classes of Members. 
There shall be two classes of members of this corporation: Dentist Members and Corporate 
Members.
Section 2. Dentist Members. 
Dentist membership in this corporation is available on an equal basis to all dentists licensed 
under Chapter 4, Articles 1 to 6, inclusive, of Division 2 of the Business and Professions Code. 
Dentist Membership shall be applied for in writing signed by the applicant and in such form 
as is prescribed by the Board of Directors and shall state the number of the license issued to 
the applicant by the Dental Board of California and contain the agreement of applicant that 
he or she shall be bound by the Articles and Bylaws of this corporation. Such application 
shall be approved for any qualified applicant unless there is evidence of facts constituting a 
basis for revocation of membership, as provided in Section 6 of this Article. As a privilege of 
membership, Dentist Members may enter into contracts with the Corporation for the provision 
of dental services as provided in Article V, Section 6(j), subject to rules and procedures 
adopted by the Board of Directors. Dentist Members may resign at any time by giving written 
notice to the corporation. A resignation, upon taking effect, terminates membership.
Section 3. Corporate Members. 
The members of the Board of Directors of this corporation shall also be the Corporate 
Members during their term of office as directors. At least sixty (60) percent of the Corporate 
Members shall be Public Members, and at least one-quarter of the Corporate Members shall 
be dentists. The membership of any Corporate Member shall terminate if his or her term 
of office as a director terminates or if he or she resigns or is removed as a director of the 
corporation.
Section 4. Voting Rights of Members. 
Unless otherwise specified in these Bylaws, any matter on which a vote of the membership 
is permitted or required by these Bylaws, by the Articles of Incorporation, or by law shall be 
approved only by affirmative vote of a majority of the Corporate Members represented at a 
duly held meeting at which a quorum is present or by written ballot pursuant to Article IV. 
Each member of this corporation shall be entitled to only one vote; provided, however, that a 
Dentist Member who is also serving as a Corporate Member shall be entitled to a vote only as 
a Corporate Member.
Section 5. Termination and Probation. 
Dentist Membership in this corporation shall terminate (1) upon forfeiture, suspension, 
revocation, surrender or failure of renewal of the dentistry license of the member; or (2) 
death of the member; or retirement from active practice; or (3) conviction of a felony or 
misdemeanor involving moral turpitude. On a determination in accordance with procedures 
adopted by the Board of Directors under Article V, Section 6(k) of the Bylaws that a member 
has violated any of the Rules for Conduct of members herein prescribed, or has been placed Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

APPENDIX A - California Provider DocumentsPage A – 9on probation by the Dental Board of California, or has had his or her license to practice 
dentistry conditioned or restricted in any way as a result of an action by the Dental Board of 
California, Delta Dental may terminate a Dentist Member’s membership in this corporation, 
or place the Dentist Member on probation and suspend or restrict the Dentist Member’s 
privileges of membership during such period of probation. The period of probation is subject 
to Delta Dental’s discretion, but shall not exceed the longer of five years, or the period of time 
during which the Dentist Member is placed on probation by the Dental Board of California 
or has his or her license conditioned or restricted as result of action by the Dental Board of 
California.
Section 6. Rules for Conduct of Dentist Members. 
The rules for the conduct of Dentist Members consist of strict conformity with the Dental 
Practice Act and prohibit the following: use of the corporate name or use of membership for 
advertising a dental practice, other than to indicate that he or she is a member; unjustifiable 
failure to complete dental care under Delta Dental plans in a reasonable period of time; gross 
immorality; violation of the Dental Practice Act; unprofessional conduct as defined in the 
Dental Practice Act; submission of false or fraudulent claims under Delta Dental group care 
contracts; willful violation of the obligation of participating dentists under such contracts, or 
failure to render professional services in accordance with the standards of dentistry in his or 
her community.
ARTICLE III — MEMBERSHIP MEETINGS
Section 1. Place of Meetings. 
Meetings of members shall be held either at the principal executive office of the corporation 
or at any other place which may be designated by the Board of Directors.
Section 2. Annual Meetings of Corporate Members. 
Written notice shall be given to each of the Corporate Members not less than thirty days in 
advance of their annual meeting specifying the time and place of such meeting.
Section 3. Special Meetings.
a. Special meetings of the Corporate Members may be called by the Board of Directors, or 
the Chair of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer, the President, or by written petition of 
five percent or more of the Corporate Members. Written notice of such meetings shall be 
given to each of the Corporate Members not less than thirty days in advance.
b. The Board of Directors may call a special meeting of the Dentist Members for the sole 
purpose of voting on a Bylaws amendment that requires approval by the Dentist Members 
pursuant to Article X, Section 1 of these Bylaws. The Secretary shall give written notice 
to all Dentist Members not less than forty-five nor more than ninety days in advance of 
the special meeting specifying the time and place of the meeting, and describing the 
proposed amendment. Such notice may be included in the regular dentist newsletter 
published by this corporation and mailed to all Dentist Members.Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

APPENDIX A - California Provider DocumentsPage A – 10Section 4. Quorum. 
Thirty Dentist Members shall constitute a quorum at a special meeting. A majority of the 
Corporate Members shall constitute a quorum at any meeting of the Corporate Members.
Section 5. Voting. 
Each member shall be entitled to one vote, personally cast, on any matter submitted to vote 
of the membership at a meeting. Proxies shall not be honored, and no cumulative voting shall 
be recognized.
Section 6. Nomination of Candidates for Corporate Members. 
The nomination and selection of Corporate Members shall be conducted as provided in Article 
V, Section 3.
ARTICLE IV — WRITTEN VOTE
Upon resolution of the Board of Directors matters may be submitted to vote of either or 
both classes of the membership outside of annual or special meetings by written ballots 
transmitted by mail or by electronic means to each member for marking and return to the 
secretary within the time specified thereon of not less than thirty days. Votes, so cast, shall 
be tabulated by the secretary and canvassed by a committee of not less than three directors 
appointed by the Board of Directors for the purpose. Business so transacted shall have the 
same force and effect as if transacted at an annual or special meeting of the membership duly 
called, provided ballots are returned by at least the number of members of a class sufficient to 
constitute a quorum if present at an annual or special meeting.
ARTICLE V—DIRECTORS
Section 1. Number and Qualifications. 
The directors of the corporation shall be not less than seven, nor more than sixteen in 
number. At least one-third of the directors shall be subscribers or enrollees entitled to receive 
dental services provided or paid for by this corporation. At least sixty (60) percent of the 
directors shall be Public Members, and at least twenty-five (25) percent of the directors shall 
be dentists. Each director shall have one vote at meetings of the Board of Directors. The 
presence of a majority of directors at a meeting regularly called shall constitute a quorum for 
the transaction of business. A majority vote of those directors present at any meeting shall 
be sufficient to pass any measure except measures on which a greater vote is required by the 
Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, or any provision of law.
Section 2. Term and Tenure.
Any person elected as a director, except to fill an unexpired term of a predecessor, shall serve 
for a period of one (1) year and until his/her successor is elected and qualified, or until his/
her earlier resignation or removal, or for additional one (1) year term(s) if reelected. The term 
of any director elected to fill an unexpired term of a predecessor shall terminate at the time at 
which the predecessor’s term would have terminated.Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

Section 7. Reserves. 
The Board of Directors shall establish a revolving or reserve fund to cover contingent 
obligations for paying dental services and anticipated future needs of the corporation which 
are reasonably likely to occur. The directors shall, in their discretion, invest so much of such 
funds in securities or other investments approved for investment of trust funds under the laws 
of the State of California as they in their discretion determine to be for the best interest of the 
corporation.
Section 8. Fees and Compensation. 
Directors, as such, shall not receive any salary for their services, but by resolution the Board 
of Directors may provide for reimbursement to themselves of expenses of attending any 
meetings of the Board or committees and may provide a fixed fee to compensate directors 
for any time in traveling to, preparing for and attending meetings of the Board of Directors or 
committees. Members of the Board of Directors are eligible to hold office in the corporation 
and receive such salary as may be fixed for that office.
Section 9. Meetings. 
A regular meeting of the Board of Directors shall be held annually in conjunction with 
the annual meeting of the Corporate Members. The time and place of meeting shall be as 
determined by the Board of Directors. Special meetings of the Board of Directors may be 
called at any time by the Chair of the Board, the Chief Executive Officer, the President or 
by any Vice Chair of the board or any five directors. Written notice of the time and place of 
such meetings shall be furnished to each director not less than five days before the time of 
meeting specified therein. In the absence of designation otherwise, the meetings of the Board 
of Directors, whether regular or special, shall be held at the principal office of the corporation 
in San Francisco. Regardless of how called, a written consent of all the members of the Board 
of Directors to the holding of a meeting of the Board filed with the minutes of the Board 
shall constitute sufficient call and notice of any meeting of the Board of Directors, and a 
meeting so held shall have the same force and effect as if the meeting were regularly called 
upon notice as hereinabove provided. A regular or special meeting of the Board of Directors, 
called in accordance with these bylaws, may be conducted, in whole or in part, by electronic 
transmission by and to the corporation, by electronic video screen communication, conference 
telephone, or other means of remote communication provided that all members consent, or 
the Board of Directors determines it is necessary or appropriate because of an emergency.Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

Any action required or permitted to be taken by the Board of Directors may be taken without

to such action. Such written consent or consents shall be filed with the minutes of the

Section 11. Quality Management Committee. 
The Board of Directors shall appoint a Quality Management Committee which shall be 
composed of not less than three, nor more than seven members; one of whom shall be the 
corporation’s executive appointive officer in charge of the corporation’s quality improvement 
and oversight function, who shall also serve as the Committee Chair without vote. The 
remainder of the Committee members shall be dentists and/or Public Members, who shall 
be appointed (or removed) by an affirmative majority vote of the Board of Directors. 
Committee members who are directors shall serve a term coterminous with their term of 
office as a director, unless such person is earlier removed from office or resigns. Committee 
members who are not directors, shall serve for a term of one year and can be re-appointed. 
The Committee Chair may serve until s/he resigns or is removed from office. The Committee 
shall meet when required to perform its functions, and shall retain any consultants, dental or 
otherwise, to advise it. A majority of the members of the Committee shall constitute a quorum 
for the transaction of business at any meeting of the Committee.

which includes oversight of the corporation’s quality plan, quality improvement workplan 
and associated quality assessment policies and processes.
b. Review and consider the appropriateness of new dental procedures for inclusion in the 
corporation’s benefit programs.
c. Periodically review the corporation’s processing policies concerning covered dental 
services.
d. Perform such other duties as are assigned to the Committee by the Board of Directors.
Section 12. Dentist Compensation Committee. 
The Dentist Compensation Committee is delegated the ultimate power and authority to 
exercise the responsibility of the Board of Directors in regard to those matters described in 
Article V, Section 6(g) of these Bylaws pertaining to establishing compensation schedules 
for professional services performed by dentists or other dental providers for which this 
corporation is obligated to make payment, which matters involve a substantial adjustment

vote of the Board of Directors. Committee members shall serve a term coterminous with

Section 13. Executive Committee.

taking of any positive action by this Committee. The Committee may act by the written or 
telephone consent of a majority of the members thereof.
c. The Executive Committee shall report to the Board of Directors any recommendations or 
actions undertaken.
ARTICLE VI — OFFICERS
Section 1. Officers. 
The officers of this corporation shall be Chair of the Board, a Chief Executive Officer, a 
President, Vice Chair(s) of the Board, a Secretary, Assistant Secretaries, Treasurer and such 
other officers the Directors may from time to time in their discretion appoint. One person may 
hold more than one office in the corporation, except that of Chair of the Board, Secretary and 
Treasurer shall each be held by a different person.
Section 2. Terms and Election. 
The Chair of the Board, Vice Chair(s) of the Board, Secretary and Treasurer shall be elected 
by the Board of Directors at an annual meeting. The Chair of the Board shall hold office for a 
minimum of three (3) years and until his/her successor is elected and qualified, or until his/
her earlier resignation or removal, or for additional one (1) year term(s) if reelected. All other 
elected officers shall hold office for one (1) year and until his/her successor is elected and 
qualified, or until his/her earlier resignation or removal, or for additional one (1) year term(s) 
if reelected. The Chair of the Board and Vice Chair(s) of the Board shall be elected from the 
membership of the Board of Directors and shall be “independent” as per the IRS Form 990 
definition. If such officer shall lose his/her independent status at any point during his/her 
term as an officer, he/she will need to resign as an officer, with a replacement elected by the Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

of any officer becomes vacant for any reason, the Board of Directors shall by majority vote 
elect a successor who shall hold office for the remainder of the unexpired term. Any officer 
may be removed during the term of his or her office by an affirmative vote of a majority of the 
Directors.
Section 3. Compensation. 
Officers of the corporation shall receive such salary as is agreed to by the Board of Directors, 
together with such allowable items of expense as are agreed to by the Board of Directors.
Section 4. Other Paid Assistants. 
The Board of Directors is authorized to engage on behalf of the corporation all necessary 
employees and assistants, including certified public accountants and attorneys at law, as 
needful or required in the advancement of the affairs of the corporation, and the Board shall 
have authority to arrange with such employees, assistants, certified public accountants and 
attorneys at law for a remuneration payable by the corporation for their services.
ARTICLE VII — DUTIES OF OFFICERS
Section 1. Chair of the Board. 
The Chair of the Board shall preside at all meetings of the membership and at all meetings 
of the Board of Directors. He or she shall be ex-officio member with voting rights of all 
committees of the Board of Directors other than the Dentist Compensation Committee and 
shall have such other and further powers and duties as may be prescribed for him or her by 
the Board of Directors or these Bylaws.
Section 2. Vice Chair of the Board. 
In the absence or disability of the Chair of the Board, the Vice Chair of the Board, in order 
of their rank as fixed by the Board of Directors, shall perform the duties of the Chair of the 
Board and when so acting the Vice Chair of the Board shall have all the powers of and all 
the responsibilities of the Chair of the Board. In addition, the Board of Directors may fix 
and assign such duties for the offices of Vice Chair of the Board as in its discretion it deems 
advisable.
Section 3. Secretary.
a. Minutes. The Secretary shall keep, or cause to be kept, a complete book of the minutes at 
the principal office of the corporation of all meetings of the Directors and of the members, 
together with all calls and notices upon which meetings were had, a roster of all members, 
including the applications for membership of each member, and record of payment or 
nonpayment of fees and assessments.
b.  Notices. The Secretary shall give, or cause to be given, the written notice of all meetings of 
membership as directed by these Bylaws and also written notice of all regular and special 
meetings of the Board of Directors of the corporation as directed by the Board, the Chief 
Executive Officer, the President, or other officers authorized to call such meetings.Bylaws of Delta Dental of California

apply the same to authenticate such instruments as are executed by the corporation and 
shall sign such instruments on behalf of the corporation as are executed by it.
Section 4. Assistant Secretaries. 
Assistant Secretaries shall perform such of the duties of the Secretary as shall from time to 
time be delegated to them by the Secretary, together with such further duties as the Board of 
Directors may assign to the offices of Assistant Secretary, and in the absence or disability of 
the Secretary or a vacancy in the office of Secretary, the Assistant Secretary shall perform all 
the duties and responsibilities of the office of Secretary.
Section 5. Treasurer. 
The Treasurer shall keep or cause to be kept adequate and correct books and accounts which 
shall show all of the funds, securities, and other proper ties of the corporation, all business 
transactions of the corporation, and all assets and liabilities, receipts and disbursements, 
reserves, revolving funds, gains, losses and other accountable items of corporate business. 
Such books shall be kept current and shall be open to inspection at all times by any officer 
or Director of the corporation. Funds of the corporation shall be deposited with such 
depositories, and shall be disbursed only upon the signatures of the officers and other 
signatories, as the Board of Directors may authorize and direct. The Board of Directors shall 
receive periodic financial reports of the affairs of the corporation. The treasurer shall have 
other powers and perform other duties as prescribed by the Board of Directors or these 
Bylaws.
Section 6. Chief Executive Officer and President. 
Subject to the Board of Directors, the Chief Executive Officer and President shall be the same 
person, unless determined by the Board of Directors that the roles should be held by different 
individuals to effectuate continuity and stability for succession purposes. The Chief Executive 
Officer and President of the corporation shall jointly and severally conduct all of the business 
affairs of the corporation, and all of its properties except as herein otherwise provided. He or 
she may be a full-time employee(s) and need not be a dental licentiate of the Dental Board of 
California. He or she shall attend all meetings of the Board of Directors and shall advise and 
consult with the Board of Directors concerning business undertakings of the corporation. The 
corporation may employ such further assistants to the Chief Executive Officer and President 
as the administration of the affairs of the corporation may require.
ARTICLE VIII – INDEMNIFICATION
Section 1. Indemnification of Directors and Officers. 
To the maximum extent permitted by law, including as applicable law may change in a way 
that expands the corporation’s power to do so, the corporation shall indemnify each of 
its directors, officers and Corporate Members against all “expenses” as defined in Section 
7237(a) of the California Corporations Code (“Code”), judgments, fines, settlements, and 
other amounts actually and reasonably incurred by them in connection with any “proceeding” 
as defined in Section 7237(a) of the Code, arising by reason of the fact that such person is or

(whether those be corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies, joint ventures,

Section 2. Payment of Expenses in Advance. 
Any expenses incurred in defending any proceeding for which indemnification is required by 
Section 1 of this Article shall be paid by the corporation in advance of the final disposition 
of the proceeding upon receipt of an undertaking, by or for the indemnitee, to repay such 
amount or the appropriate portion of such amount if it ultimately is determined that the 
indemnitee is not entitled to be indemnified (or in part not entitled to be indemnified) as 
required or authorized by this Article VIII.
Section 3. Indemnity Not Exclusive. 
The indemnification and advancement of defense expenses provided by this Article VIII shall 
not be considered exclusive of any other rights to which those seeking indemnification or 
advances of defense expenses may be entitled under any properly authorized agreement.
Section 4. Insurance. 
The corporation shall have the power to purchase and maintain insurance on behalf of 
any person who is or was a director, officer, Corporate Member, employee or agent of the 
corporation against any liability asserted against or incurred by that person in that capacity 
or any of the other capacities referred to in Section 1 of this Article VIII. That insurance 
may include coverage for liabilities for which the corporation does not have the power to 
indemnify that person. The corporation shall also have the power to purchase and maintain 
insurance for the corporation itself respecting its indemnification of such persons and its 
advancement of defense expenses to or for such persons.
ARTICLE IX — SEAL
The corporation shall have a seal consisting of two concentric circles with the words, “Delta 
Dental of California’’ inscribed in the area between the two circles and the words and figures 
‘‘Incorporated State of California, May 31, 1955,’’ within the inner of two circles.

Revised as of January 1, 2025
1. Application.
  These procedures are adopted pursuant to the Delta Dental of California (“Delta”) 
Bylaws. These procedures shall apply in any case in which the Vice President 
and Chief Dental Officer propose that Delta initiate an action, including a denial , 
probation, or termination, against a Dentist Member and/or Participating Provider for 
a medical disciplinary cause or reason.
2. Definitions.
 A.  Dentist Member: A dentist who holds a Dentist Membership as defined in, and in 
accordance with, the applicable Bylaws.
 B.  Participating Provider: A dentist or dental specialist who has entered into any 
written participating agreement (“Participating Provider Agreement”) or a dentist 
or dental specialist, credentialed and approved for Network participation pursuant 
to a Practice Agreement.
 C.  Practice Agreement: A written agreement entered into by a TIN-holding entity for 
the provision of dental services.
 D.  Medical Disciplinary Cause or Reason: As used in these procedures, that aspect 
of a dentist’s competence or professional conduct which is reasonably likely to be 
detrimental to patient safety or to the delivery of patient care.
 E.  Medical Disciplinary Action: A definitive medical disciplinary action taken against a 
Dentist Member or Participating Provider.
3. Immediate Action.
Notwithstanding the procedures set forth below, the Vice President and Chief 
Dental Officer may immediately initiate an action against a Dentist Member and/or 
Participating Provider for a medical disciplinary cause or reason where the failure to 
take such action may result in imminent danger to the health of any individual, provided 
that the Dentist Member and/or Participating Provider is subsequently provided with 
the notice and hearing rights set forth below.
4. Notice of Medical Disciplinary Action.
Upon the recommendation of the Vice President and Chief Dental Officer, written notice 
shall be given to the Dentist Member and/or Participating Provider (“Respondent“) 
informing Respondent of:
 a. the final proposed action;
 b.  the reason for the final proposed action, including the acts or omissions with 
which Respondent is charged;
 c.   the effective date of the final proposed action, which date shall be at least thirty 
(30) days from the date of the notice of final proposed action;
d.  the requirement that the final proposed action be reported to the Dental Board of 
California pursuant to Section 805 of the Business and Professions Code;
 e.  the right of Respondent to request and participate in a hearing to challenge the 
basis for Delta’s proposed action by delivering such request to Delta prior to the 
effective date of the final proposed action.

APPENDIX A - California Provider DocumentsPage A – 21 f.  the right of the Respondent, prior to requesting a hearing, to submit a written 
appeal to challenge the basis for Delta’s proposed action, including any materials 
refuting the basis of the proposed termination, and a detailed explanation of 
Respondent’s position. Respondent’s written submission must be delivered to the 
enterprise prior to the effective date of the proposed termination. The enterprise 
shall review any written materials that are timely submitted by Respondent and 
issue its final decision within thirty (30) days of Respondent’s written appeal. If 
Respondent is dissatisfied with the outcome of the written appeal, Respondent 
may still request a hearing, consistent with “e” above; and
 g.    the procedure governing medical disciplinary hearings, including that the failure 
of Respondent to submit a written appeal or to request a hearing within the time 
required shall result in a waiver of Respondent’s right to a hearing and Delta 
shall initiate the final proposed action on the effective date. Respondent will be 
deemed to have waived their right to appeal the proposed termination and there 
will be no further right to an administrative appeal.
5. Notice of Hearing.
If a hearing is requested in writing by Respondent within the time specified in Section 
4(e), within a reasonable time, written notice shall be given to Respondent providing 
Respondent with:
a.  the place, time and date of the hearing, which date shall be no more than sixty 
(60) days or less than thirty (30) days after receipt of the request for the hearing;
b.  a list of witnesses (if any) expected to testify at the hearing on behalf of Delta;
c.  the reason for the final proposed action, including the acts or omissions with 
which Respondent is charged;
d.  copies of any non-privileged documents relevant to the final proposed action 
which Delta has in Its possession or under its control;
e.  a request that copies of any non-privileged documents relevant to the final 
proposed action which Respondent has in his or her possession or under his or her 
control be furnished for inspection and copying by Delta within fifteen (15) days 
after receipt of the notice of the hearing;
f.  the names, credentials and backgrounds of at least three (3) licensed dentists to 
serve as members of the Dental Quality Hearing Panel (“Panel”), which is the trier 
of fact at the hearing;
g.  the name, credentials and background of a licensed attorney to serve as a non- 
voting officer at the hearing (“Hearing Officer”); and
h.  advisement that at Delta’s option, any or all hearing sessions may be conducted 
by virtual video conference platform instead of in person. When hearing sessions 
are conducted by virtual video conference, all hearing participants, including 
the parties, the Hearing Officer, the Panel Members, the witnesses, and the court 
reporter may attend the hearing sessions remotely, so long as all participants, 
including the parties, the Hearing Officer, the Panel Members, the witnesses, 
and the court reporter can see each other, can hear and be heard during the 
proceedings, and have access to all evidence admitted at the hearing, either by 
electronic means or hard copies. The Hearing Officer has authority and discretion 
to rule on questions regarding the implementation of the virtual proceedings.California Medical Disciplinary Hearing Procedures (continued)

APPENDIX A - California Provider DocumentsPage A – 226. Hearing Panel/Hearing Officer/Challenges/Postponement.
Delta shall propose at least three (3) licensed dentists to serve as members of the 
Dental Quality Hearing Panel (“Panel”) which shall be the trier of fact at the hearing. The 
Panel shall include, where feasible, a dentist practicing the same recognized specialty 
as Respondent. The Hearing Officer shall be a licensed attorney who shall not act as 
a prosecuting officer and shall not be entitled to vote. Members of the Panel and the 
Hearing Officer may not concurrently serve as an officer or employee of Delta Dental 
of California or any of its affiliated companies, or have acted as an accuser, investigator, 
fact finder or initial decision maker in the matter before the Panel, or gain a direct 
financial benefit from the outcome of the matter.
Respondent shall have the right, prior to the hearing, to question and challenge the 
impartiality of any member of the Panel and the Hearing Officer. A request to question 
any Panel Member and/or the Hearing Officer must be made within ten (10) days of 
receipt of the notice of hearing given in accordance with Section 5. The parties will work 
together, along with the Hearing Officer where appropriate, to schedule a date for the 
voir dire to occur prior to the hearing date. Challenges to the impartiality of any Panel 
Member or Hearing Officer shall be ruled on by the Hearing Officer. Should the hearing 
date need to be rescheduled to accommodate scheduling a voir dire session, the date 
of the voir dire session shall be considered the first date of the hearing for purposes of 
compliance with the timing requirements of scheduling the hearing.
If a challenge to any Panel Member is sustained, there must be at least two (2) dentists 
remaining on the Panel to hear and decide the matter. In the event that successful 
challenges to impartiality result in the disqualification of the Hearing Officer or in less 
than two (2) dentists remaining on the Panel, the hearing shall be postponed.
Delta shall then provide the names, credentials, and backgrounds of a new Hearing 
Officer and/or additional dentists sufficient to constitute a Panel of at least three (3) 
dentists. Respondent shall have a reasonable opportunity to question and challenge 
the new Hearing Officer and/or the additional Panel members prior to the postponed 
hearing which shall be scheduled no later than sixty (60) days after the original hearing 
date.
Postponement of the hearing date shall otherwise be granted only upon mutual 
agreement of the parties or for good cause as determined in writing by the Hearing 
Officer, or pursuant to this policy or applicable law. Failure of Delta or Respondent to 
comply in a timely manner with any action required by these procedures shall constitute 
good cause for a postponement if requested by the party prejudiced by the failure to 
comply.

Delta is likewise entitled to inspect, copy, or access any documentary information 
relevant to the charges, which Respondent has in his/her possession or control which

each party shall have:
a. access to all information made available to the Panel;
b. the right to call, examine and cross-examine witnesses;
c. the right to present and rebut relevant evidence; and

Rulings on the admissibility of evidence shall be made by the Hearing Officer without

whether a document or testimony is admissible, the Hearing Officer shall consider the 
relevancy, purpose and probative value of the evidence.
10. Burden of Proof.
a.  Delta shall bear the burden of proof in persuading the Panel by a preponderance 
of the evidence that the action proposed to be taken against a Respondent who 
is an existing Dentist Member and/or Participating Provider is reasonable and 
warranted.
b.  A Respondent who is an applicant to become a Dentist Member and/or 
Participating Provider shall bear the burden of proof by a preponderance of the 
evidence of his qualification by producing information which allows for a dequate 
evaluation and resolution of reasonable doubts concerning qualifications to 
become a Dentist Member and/or Participating Provider.
c.  An applicant Respondent shall not be permitted to introduce information not

The hearing shall be completed within a reasonable time. After each party has had 
a sufficient opportunity to present its case, including the submission of a written 
statement at the close of the hearing, the Panel shall retire to decide the matter.
Each matter shall be decided by the vote of a majority of the Panel. In the event of a tie 
vote of an even-numbered Panel, the matter shall be decided in favor of Respondent. 
The Panel shall provide a written decision, including findings of fact and a conclusion 
articulating the connection between the evidence produced at the hearing and the 
decision reached. The written decision shall be given to Delta and sent by Delta to the 
Respondent. There shall be no administrative appeal from the decision of the Panel. 
Delta shall initiate the final proposed action if the decision affirms the final proposed 
action. Delta shall initiate action in accordance with the decision if the decision 
overrules or modifies the final proposed action. A decision of the Panel shall not be 
appealable except by a petition for a writ of mandate made to the California Superior 
Court within one year of the decision.

certified mail or overnight mail, sent to the Respondent at the latest address shown on 
the records of Delta or through search of reasonably and publicly available sources or 
to the Respondent’s counsel by certified mail or overnight mail. Any notice or written 
communication to Delta or any officer of Delta will be sent to the physical and/or 
electronic address shown on the notice of action given in accordance with Section 4,  
or to Delta’s counsel by overnight mail or electronic mail.California Medical Disciplinary Hearing Procedures (continued)

1. Application. 
This policy is adopted pursuant to the Delta Dental of California Bylaws. Except as 
provided in Section 2, this policy shall apply to the following actions (“CTAP Actions” as
