of a dentist’s competence or professional conduct which is reasonably likely to 
be detrimental to a patient’s safety or to the delivery of patient care for which a 
report is required to be filed with the Dental Board pursuant to Section 805 of the 
Business and Professions Code; and
b.  Termination of a Participating Provider Agreement, Practice Agreement, Network 
Participation, or Dentist Membership because of death or retirement from active 
practice; and
c.  Other (non-termination) provider disputes subject to the Provider Dispute 
Resolution Mechanism.
3. Definitions. 
The following terms shall have the meanings stated:
a.  “Dentist Member” means a dentist who holds a Dentist Membership in Delta as 
defined in, and in accordance with the Delta Dental of California Bylaws.
b.  “Participating Provider” means a dentist or dental specialist who has entered into 
any written participating agreement (“Participating Provider Agreement”) or a 
dentist or dental specialist credentialed and approved for Network participation 
pursuant to a Practice Agreement.
c.  “Practice Agreement” means a written agreement entered into by a TIN-holding 
entity for the provision of dental services.
d.  “California Termination Action Policy (“CTAP”) Action” means an action taken 
against a Dentist Member, Participating Provider, or Practice pursuant to the 
California Termination Action Policy.
e.  “CTAP Action Committee” means the Committee that reviews a Termination 
Action pursuant to a timely appeal. It shall consist of at least two (2) Dentist 
Members and one (1) corporate member of Delta appointed by the Chairman 
of the Board of Directors. The Chairman may also appoint alternate Committee 
members to serve in the event an appointed Committee member is unable to 
serve or is disqualified for any reason prior to a decision.
 1 Applicable to a dentist or dental specialist credentialed and approved for Network participation pursuant to a

APPENDIX A - California Provider DocumentsPage A – 264. Grounds for CTAP Actions. 
Delta may place a Participating Provider/Dentist Member on probation or terminate 
a Participating Provider Agreement/Dentist Membership, Practice Agreement, or a 
Participating Provider’s Network Participation for violation of any of the terms, rules, 
or policies referenced in the Participating Dentist Agreement or Bylaws, or if Delta has 
reason to believe the dentist(s) do not abide by such terms, rules, or policies.
5. Initiation of Termination Actions. 
A CTAP Action may be initiated against a Dentist Member, Participating Provider, 
or Practice (“Respondent”) by the President or any corporate officer or employee 
designated by the President by mailing written notice of the nature, effective date and 
factual basis for the CTAP Action along with a copy of this policy to the Respondent, 
including the licensed dentist or other authorized individual specified in the Practice 
Agreement, as applicable, to receive Notices and communications, at least thirty (30) 
days before the effective date of the CTAP Action. The notice shall also advise the 
Respondent that Delta shall review and consider any and all written materials presented 
by Respondent to refute, disprove, or challenge the basis for the CTAP Action, if 
received by Delta prior to the effective date. If no written materials are presented, the 
CTAP Action shall be effective on the date stated in the notice of proposed termination 
letter, and there shall be no further right to administrative review or appeal of the  
CTAP Action.
6. Review of CTAP Actions. 
Any written materials presented by the Respondent prior to the effective date of the 
CTAP Action shall be reviewed and considered by Delta. Delta may request that the 
Respondent provide additional evidence. The Respondent may request additional 
non-privileged information and/or documents from Delta which Delta may provide 
if the request is deemed reasonable or compliance with the request is not unduly 
burdensome. Within forty-five (45) days of receipt of evidence presented by the 
Respondent, the written decision of the President or another officer of Delta designated 
by the President shall be mailed to the Respondent. The CTAP Action shall be overruled 
or modified only if the Respondent successfully refutes, challenges, or disproves the 
basis for the CTAP Action.
7. Appeal to CTAP Action Committee (“Committee”). 
The Respondent may appeal the decision of Delta made pursuant to Section 6 to 
the Committee by filing with the Secretary of Delta, within ten (10) days after receipt 
of the decision, a notice of appeal and a written statement of the reasons why the 
Respondent disagrees with the decision. The Respondent may submit additional 
materials and/or request that the Committee conduct a hearing with the Respondent 
present by including such request in the notice of appeal; the Committee shall decide 
by majority vote whether to grant or deny a request for hearing with the Respondent 
present and shall provide said decision within fifteen (15) days of the notice of appeal. 
In addition, within fifteen (15) days of the date of receipt of the notice of appeal, 
Delta shall forward to each member of the Committee the written evidence of Delta 
in support of the CTAP Action, the written materials previously presented by the 
Respondent to Delta, the decision of Delta, the Respondent’s notice of appeal and 
written statement of the reasons why the Respondent disagrees with Delta’s decision, 
and any additional relevant materials. Should the Committee deny a request for a 
hearing with the Respondent present, the Committee shall, nonetheless, hold (either in 
person, telephonically, or using other remote communications technology) a hearing California Termination Action Policy  (continued)

or evidence, and render a decision. Failure to timely appeal to the Committee as

based solely upon the written materials provided to the Committee as discussed above.

In the event the Committee decides to conduct a hearing with the Respondent present, 
the following rules shall govern Committee hearings:
a.  The Respondent shall be given at least thirty (30) days’ notice by the Secretary of 
Delta of the time and place of the hearing.
b.  The hearing shall be held within seventy-five (75) days of the date of the notice of 
appeal unless postponed by mutual agreement of Delta and the Respondent.
c.  At Delta’s option, any or all hearing sessions may be conducted by virtual video 
conference platform instead of in person. When hearing sessions are conducted 
by virtual video conference, all hearing participants, including the parties, the 
Hearing Officer, the Panel Members, the witnesses, and the court reporter may 
attend the hearing sessions remotely, so long as all participants, including the 
Respondent, the Committee Members, and the Hearing Officer can see each 
other, can hear and be heard during the proceedings, and have access to all 
evidence admitted at the hearing, either by electronic means or hard copies. The 
Hearing Officer has authority and discretion to rule on questions regarding the 
implementation of the virtual proceedings.
d.  Delta shall furnish a stenographic reporter or electronic recording equipment to 
record the hearing proceedings.
e.  The Committee may have a hearing officer to advise it concerning the hearing 
procedure.
f.  The Committee shall consider the written submissions provided to it and such 
additional evidence as may be offered at the hearing. The Committee need not 
be bound by legal rules of evidence but may consider any evidence of the sort on 
which responsible persons are accustomed to rely in the conduct of serious affairs. 
The Committee need not consider evidence which is merely cumulative or which it 
determines is not relevant to the issues raised by the CTAP Action.
g.  The Respondent may request that Delta produce documents in its custody or 
control or produce as witnesses persons employed by Delta. Delta likewise shall 
have a right to request production of documents or witnesses by the Respondent.

hearing and each party shall fully and completely comply with such request no 
later than fifteen (15) days prior to the hearing date. The Committee may, in its 
discretion, disregard documents or witnesses not timely produced or identified by 
either party as described herein.California Termination Action Policy  (continued)

ARTICLE 1.0
Section 1.0 The name of the Corporation is Delta Dental of the District of Columbia.
ARTICLE 2.0
Purposes
Section 2.0 In furtherance of the purpose for which the Corporation is formed as set 
forth in its Certificate of Incorporation, the objectives of the Corporation shall be:
Section 2.1 To increase the availability of dental services to the public by encouraging 
the expansion of dental prepayment plans administered through a non-profit service 
Corporation, and to provide the means for active association group coverage programs 
on behalf of buyers and providers of dental care; and to assist in prevention and 
eradication of dental disease by providing responsible dental benefits to the public at 
reasonable costs.
ARTICLE 3.0
Corporate Membership
Section 3.0 Composition: The corporate members shall be the Board of Directors of 
Dentegra Group, Inc., a nonprofit corporation organized under the laws of Delaware. Any 
person who ceases to be a director of Dentegra Group, Inc. shall cease to be a member 
of the Corporation.
Section 3.1 Duties of Corporate Members: The corporate members shall elect the 
directors as hereinafter provided and shall perform such other duties and exercise such 
other rights and powers as are provided by law or by these Bylaws.
Section 3.2 Duties of Corporate Members Concerning Management and Service Mark 
Agreements: The corporate members shall approve the Corporation’s entering into or 
terminating or assigning management agreements, including but not limited to General 
Agency Agreements with Delta Dental of Pennsylvania and Delta Dental Insurance 
Company, and agreements concerning the use of the Delta Dental service marks, 
including but not limited to the Affiliate Service Mark License Agreement with Delta 
Dental Plans Association before the Corporation shall take such actions.
Section 3.3 Duties of Corporate Members Concerning Dissolution, Merger or 
Consolidation: The corporate members shall approve any dissolution, merger or 
consolidation of the Corporation before the Corporation shall take such actions.
ARTICLE 4.0
Meetings of Corporate Members
Section 4.0 Meetings: Meetings of the corporate members shall be in accordance with 
the Bylaws provisions of Dentegra Group, Inc. concerning meetings of directors.

not less than three (3) nor more than seven (7) natural persons of full age, of either sex.
Section 5.1 Election and Tenure: Any person elected as a director, except to fill an 
unexpired term of a predecessor, shall serve for a period of one year, or until a successor 
is elected. The term of any director elected to fill an unexpired term of a predecessor 
shall terminate at the time at which the predecessor’s term would have terminated.
Section 5.2 Forfeiture: The term of any director shall terminate if s/he shall fail to attend 
two consecutive meetings of the directors without good cause. The majority of the 
remaining directors shall have sole authority to determine what shall constitute “good 
cause” for absence from the meeting.
Section 5.3 Composition of Board of Directors: The directors who are not Dentists (lay 
members) shall exceed the number of directors who are Participating Dentists by at 
least one.
Section 5.4 Election of Directors: The corporate members shall elect directors to serve 
for terms as described in Section 5.1.
Section 5.5 Selection of Directors: The Secretary of Dentegra Group, Inc. shall nominate 
persons to the Corporate Membership to fill a vacancy among the directors.
Section 5.6 Resignation/Removal of Directors and Filling of Vacancies:

resignation to be made in writing directed to the Board of Directors.

provisions of a law, these Bylaws or policies adopted by the Board of Directors, 
only upon the affirmative vote of a majority of the other directors and a concurring 
resolution of the Membership.
c.  Vacancies in the Board of Directors, including vacancies caused by the resignation 
or removal of directors pursuant to this Section, may be filled by election by the 
Corporate Members of an eligible person, to serve until the next regular meeting of 
the directors.

Directors without vote.

or without the District of Columbia, at such time and such place as shall be determined 
by the Board of Directors for other business as may properly come before said meeting.

Directors shall be sent to each director at least ten (10) days prior thereto. Notice of the 
time, place and purpose of other meetings shall be sent to each director not less than 
two (2) days prior to the day named for the meeting.

or special meeting by, or conduct the meeting through the use of any means of 
communication by which all directors participating may simultaneously hear each other 
during the meeting. A director participating in a meeting by this means is deemed to be 
present in person at the meeting.Bylaws of Delta Dental of the District of Columbia (continued)

Dentists
Section 9.0 Definition: The term “Dentist” or “Provider” as used by these Bylaws, or 
any other document pertaining to this Corporation, shall include any Doctor of Dental 
Surgery or Doctor of Dental Medicine duly licensed by any United States governmental 
authority to practice dentistry. The terms “Participating Dentist” or “Participating 
Provider” as used in these Bylaws or any other document pertaining to this Corporation, 
shall mean a Dentist or Provider who is licensed in the District of Columbia and has 
executed a Participating Dentist Agreement or Participating Provider Agreement.
Section 9.1 Participation: Every dentist duly licensed within the area(s) covered by this 
Corporation shall have the right to contract as a Participating Dentist to provide dental 
services to the Corporation’s subscribers, subject to meeting the Corporation’s rules for 
participation, which the Corporation may amend from time to time. Notwithstanding the 
preceding sentence, the Corporation may terminate a Participating Dentist’s contract 
after giving the Dentist due notice and an opportunity for administrative review in 
accordance with the Corporation’s policies and procedures. No Participating Dentist 
may use any Delta Dental service mark without the Corporation’s permission.
Section 9.2 Diagnosis and Treatment: Neither this Corporation, nor any member of 
its Board of Directors, its officers, employees, agents, or Committees shall impose any 
restrictions on Dentists who administer to its subscribers as to methods of diagnosis 
and treatment. The relationship between a subscriber and Dentist treating him or her 
shall be identical with the relationship that ordinarily exists in the community between a 
Dentist and his or her patient.
Section 9.3 Binding Nature of Subscriber Contracts and Dentist Handbook: Every 
Participating Dentist shall be bound by any contract entered into by the Corporation (as 
approved by the Insurance Commissioner of District of Columbia) insofar as the contract 
dictates the services to be rendered to subscribers, the fees to be paid therefor, and any 
other matter pertaining to the obligation of the Corporation to the subscriber. Every 
Participating Dentist shall also be bound by the Dentist Handbook issued by and which 
may be revised from time to time by the Corporation.
Section 9.4 Reports: Participating Dentists shall furnish to the Corporation all reports 
required by action of the Board of Directors or by any officer or other representative of 
the Corporation acting under the authority of the Board of Directors.

to carry professional liability insurance with minimum coverage limitations of at least 
$500,000/$1 million which level shall be reviewed from time to time by the Corporation 
for reasonableness and accessibility.

Any references to Usual Customary and Reasonable Fee (UCR) in Participating Dentist 
Agreements shall be changed to Maximum Plan Allowance (MPA) and Allowed Amount 
as those terms are substituted for UCR in dental service contracts, in regulating the 
services to be rendered to subscribers, the fees to be paid therefor, and any other 
matter pertaining to the obligation of the Corporation to a subscriber.Bylaws of Delta Dental of the District of Columbia (continued)

Indemnification of Officers, Directors and Employees
Section 1. Standard of Conduct Qualifying for Indemnification. The Corporation shall 
shall indemnify each person, his/her heirs, executors and administrators, who is or 
was a director, officer or employee of the Corporation or another corporation which 
he/she served as such at the request of the Corporation, against any and all liability 
and reasonable expense that may be incurred by him in connection with or resulting 
from any claim, action, suit or proceeding (whether brought by or in the right of the 
Corporation or such other corporation or otherwise), civil, criminal, administrative 
or legislative, or in connection with an appeal relating thereto in which he/she may 
become involved, as a party or otherwise, by reason of his/her being or having been 
a director, officer or employee of the Corporation or such other corporation, or by 
reason of any past or future action taken or not taken in his/her capacity as such 
director, officer or employee, whether or not he/she continues to be such at the time 
such liability or expense is incurred, provided such person acted in good faith, in what 
he/she reasonably believed to be the best interest of the Corporation or such other 
corporation, as the case be, and, in addition, in any criminal action, or proceeding, had 
no reasonable cause to believe that his/her conduct was unlawful.
Section 2. Definition of Liability and Expense. As used in this Article, the terms 
“liability” and “expense” shall include, but shall not be limited to, counsel fees and 
disbursements and amounts of judgments, fines, penalties against, and amounts 
paid in settlement by, a director, officer or employee, other than amounts paid to the 
Corporation itself or to such other corporation served at the Corporation’s request.
Section 3. Effect of Favorable Court Decision. Any such director, officer or employee, 
who has been wholly successful, on the merits or otherwise, with respect to any claim, 
suit or proceeding of the character described herein, shall be entitled to indemnification 
as of right.
Section 4. Effect of Finding of Recklessness or Willful Misconduct. Indemnification 
pursuant to this Article shall not be made in any case where the act or failure to act 
giving rise to the claim for indemnification is determined by a court to have constituted 
willful misconduct or recklessness.
Section 5. Effect of Adverse Court Decision without Finding of Willful Misconduct or 
Recklessness. The termination of any claim, action, suit or proceeding, civil or criminal, 
by judgment, settlement (whether with or without court approval) or conviction or upon 
a plea of guilty or of nolo contendere, or its equivalent shall not create a presumption 
that a director, officer or employee did not meet the standards of conduct set forth 
in Section 1 of this Article, except where there shall have been a judgment rendered 
specifically finding that the action or conduct of such director, officer or employee 
referred to in this Article constituted willful misconduct or recklessness.
Section 6. Procedure for Obtaining Indemnification. Any indemnification under this 
Article, shall be made at the discretion of the Corporation, but only if (1) the Board of 
Directors, acting by a majority vote of a quorum consisting of directors who are not 
parties to (or have been wholly successful with respect to) such claim, action, suit or 
proceeding, shall find that the director, officer or employee has met the standards of 
conduct set forth in Section 1 of this Article, or (2) independent legal counsel (who may 
be the regular counsel of the Corporation), shall deliver to it their written advice that, in 
their opinion, such director, officer or employee has met such standards.Bylaws of Delta Dental of Delaware, Inc. (continued)

accountability prior to said subject matter being introduced to the full Board of

ARTICLE IX
Executive Committee
Section 1. Composition. The Executive Committee shall consist of the Vice Chair, the 
Secretary and Treasurer of the Corporation, the Chair of the Finance Committee, the 
Chair of the Nominating Committee, the Chair of the Audit Committee and such other 
directors of the Board of Directors as the Chair of the Board may from time to time 
designate. The Immediate Past Chair, the Chair of the Board and the President shall 
be ex officio members without vote. The Chair of the Board shall be the Chair of the 
Executive Committee. The Executive Committee shall meet at the call of the Chair of the 
Board.

the powers of the Board of Directors when the Board of Directors is not in session, 
excepting such powers as may, by law or by these Bylaws, be required to be exercised

may expressly reserve to itself.

shall be necessary to the taking of any positive action by this Committee.

of the members thereof, although not formally convened.

of its proceedings and report the same to the Board of Directors at each meeting 
thereof.

of its Chair.Bylaws of Delta Dental of Pennsylvania  (continued)

ARTICLE XIII
Dentists
Section 1. Definition. The terms “Dentist” and “Provider” as used in these Bylaws or 
any other document pertaining to this Corporation, shall include any Doctor of Dental 
Surgery or Doctor of Dental Medicine duly licensed by any government authority to 
practice dentistry. The terms “Participating Dentist” or “Participating Provider” as used

time. Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, the Corporation may refuse to contract 
with or terminate the contract of any Participating Dentist or Participating Provider 
after due notice and an opportunity for administrative review in accordance with the 
Corporation’s policies and procedures. The Corporation will notify the Department 
of Health of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania when terminating a Pennsylvania 
Participating Dentist’s or Participating Provider’s contract, as required by law. No 
Participating Dentist or Participating Provider may use any Delta Dental service mark 
without the Corporation’s permission.

Board of Directors, its officers, employees, agents, or Committees shall impose any 
restrictions on Dentists or Providers who administer to its subscribers as to methods of 
diagnosis or treatment. The relationship between a subscriber and Dentist or Provider 
treating him/her shall be identical with the relationship that ordinarily exists in the 
community between a Dentist or Provider and his/her patient.Bylaws of Delta Dental of Pennsylvania  (continued)

Dentists and Participating Providers who treat subscribers in the Corporation’s dental

ARTICLE XV
Indemnification of Officers, Directors and Employees
Section 1. Standard of Conduct Qualifying for Indemnification. The Corporation shall 
indemnify each person, his/her heirs, executors and administrators, who is or was a 
director, officer or employee of the Corporation or another corporation which he served 
as such at the request of the Corporation, against any and all liability and reasonable 
expense that may be incurred by him/her in connection with or resulting from any claim, 
action, suit or proceeding (whether brought by or in the right of the Corporation or 
such other corporation or otherwise), civil, criminal, administrative or legislative, or in 
connection with an appeal relating thereto in which he may become involved, as a party 
or otherwise, by reason of his/her being or having been a director, officer or employee 
of the Corporation or such other corporation, or by reason of any past or future action 
taken or not taken in his/her capacity as such director, officer or employee, whether 
or not he/she continues to be such at the time such liability or expense is incurred, 
provided such person acted in good faith, in what he/she reasonably believed to be 
the best interest of the Corporation or such other corporation, as the case be, and, in 
addition, in any criminal action, or proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe that 
his/her conduct was unlawful.
Section 2. Definition of Liability and Expense. As used in this Article, the terms 
“liability” and “expense” shall include, but shall not be limited to, counsel fees and 
disbursements and amount of judgments, fines, penalties against, and amounts paid 
in settlement by, a director, officer or employee, other than amounts paid to the 
Corporation itself or to such other corporation served at the Corporation’s request.
Section 3. Effect of Favorable Court Decision. Any such director, officer or employee, 
who has been wholly successful, on the merits or otherwise, with respect to any claim, 
suit or proceeding of the character described herein, shall be entitled to indemnification 
as of right.
Section 4. Effect of Finding of Recklessness or Willful Misconduct. Indemnification 
pursuant to this Article shall not be made in any case where the act or failure to act 
giving rise to the claim for indemnification is determined by a court to have constituted 
willful misconduct or recklessness.
Section 5. Effect of Adverse Court Decision without Finding of Willful Misconduct or 
Recklessness. The termination of any claim, action, suit or proceeding, civil or criminal, 
by judgment, settlement (whether with or without court approval) or conviction or upon 
a plea of guilty or of nolo contendere, or its equivalent shall not create a presumption 
that a director, officer or employee did not meet the standards of conduct set forth 
in Section 1 of this Article, except where there shall have been a judgment rendered 
specifically finding that the action or conduct of such director, officer or employee 
referred to in this Article constituted willful misconduct or recklessness.Bylaws of Delta Dental of Pennsylvania  (continued)

OFFICERS

designated, the Board of Directors may, from time to time, elect, or appoint such other 
officers or agents as the Board of Directors shall deem necessary or appropriate and 
may prescribe their respective powers and duties.Bylaws of Delta Dental Plan of West Virginia, Inc. (continued)

APPENDIX B - Mid-Atlantic BylawsARTICLE SEVEN
INDEMNIFICATION OF DIRECTORS, OFFICERS OR EMPLOYEES
1. Standard of Conduct Qualifying for Indemnification: The Corporation shall indemnify 
each person, his/her heirs, executors and administrators, who is or was a director, officer 
or employee of the Corporation or another corporation which he served as such at the 
request of the Corporation, against any and all liability and reasonable expense that 
may be incurred by him/her in connection with or resulting from any claim, action, suit, 
or proceeding (whether brought by or in the right of the Corporation or such other 
corporation or otherwise), civil, criminal, administrative or legislative, or in connection 
with an appeal relating thereto in which he/she may become involved, as a party or 
otherwise, by reason of his/her being or having been a director, officer or employee of 
the Corporation or such other corporation, or by reason of any past or future action 
taken or not taken in his/her capacity as such director, officer or employee, whether 
or not he/she continues to be such at the time such liability or expense is incurred, 
provided such person acted in good faith, in what he/she reasonably believed to be the 
best interest of the Corporation or such other corporation, as the case may be, and in 
addition, in any criminal action, or proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe that 
this conduct was unlawful.
2. Definition of Liability and Expense: As used in this Article, the terms “liability” and 
“expense” shall include, but shall not be limited to, counsel fees and disbursements and 
amounts of judgments, fines, penalties against, and amounts paid in settlement by a 
director, officer or employee, other than amounts paid to the Corporation itself or to 
such other corporation served at the Corporation’s request.
3. Effect of Favorable Court Decision: Any such director, officer or employee, who has 
been wholly successful, on the merits or otherwise, with respect to any claim, suit or 
proceeding of the character described herein, shall be entitled to indemnification as of 
right.
4. Effect of Finding of Recklessness or Willful Misconduct: Indemnification pursuant 
to this Article shall not be made in any case where the act or failure to act giving rise 
to the claim for indemnification is determined by a court to have constituted willful 
misconduct or recklessness.
5. Effect of Adverse Court Decision Without Finding of Willful Misconduct or 
Recklessness. The termination of any claim, action, suit or proceeding, civil or criminal, 
by judgment, settlement (whether with or without court approval) or conviction or upon 
a plea of guilty or of nolo contendere, or its equivalent shall not create a presumption 
that a director, officer or employee did not meet the standards of conduct set forth 
in Section 1 of this Article, except where there shall have been a judgment rendered 
specifically finding that the action of conduct of such director, officer or employee 
referred to in this Article constituted willful misconduct or recklessness.
6. Procedure for Obtaining Indemnification: Any indemnification under this Article shall 
be made by the Corporation, but only if (1) the Board of Directors acting by a majority 
vote of the quorum consisting of directors who are not parties to (or have been wholly 
successful with respect to) such claim, action, suit or proceeding, shall find that the 
director, officer or employee has met the standards of conduct set forth in Section 1 of 
this Article, or (2) independent legal counsel (who may be the regular counsel of the 
Corporation), shall deliver to it their written advice that, in their opinion, such director, 
officer or employee has met such standards.Bylaws of Delta Dental Plan of West Virginia, Inc. (continued)

APPENDIX B - Mid-Atlantic Bylaws7. Payment of Expenses Before Final Disposition: Expenses incurred with respect to any 
claim, action, suit or proceeding described in Section 1 of this Article may be advanced 
by the Corporation prior to the final disposition thereof upon receipt of any undertaking 
by or on behalf of the recipient to repay such amount unless it shall ultimately be 
determined that he/she is entitled to indemnification under this Article.
8. Right of Indemnification Not Exclusive: The rights of indemnification provided in this 
Article shall be in addition to any rights to which any person concerned may otherwise 
be entitled by contract or as a matter of law, by vote of directors or members or 
otherwise both as to actions of officers, directors or employees in their official capacity 
or in another capacity while in office and whether or not the indemnified liability arises 
or arose from any threatened, pending or completed activity by or in the right of the 
Corporation.
ARTICLE EIGHT
DENTISTS
1. Definition: The terms “Dentist” or “Provider” as used in these Bylaws or any other 
document pertaining to this Corporation, shall include any Doctor of Dental Surgery 
or Doctor of Dental Medicine duly licensed by any governmental authority to practice 
dentistry. The terms “Participating Dentist” or “Participating Provider” as used in these 
Bylaws or any other document pertaining to this Corporation, shall mean a Dentist or 
Provider who is licensed in the state of West Virginia and has executed a Participating 
Dentist Agreement or Participating Provider Agreement.
2. Participation: Every Dentist duly licensed within the area(s) covered by this 
Corporation shall have the right to contract as a Participating Dentist to provide dental 
services to the Corporation’s subscribers, subject to meeting the Corporation’s rules for 
participation, which the Corporation may amend from time to time. Notwithstanding the 
preceding sentence, the Corporation may terminate a Participating Dentist’s contract 
after giving the Dentist due notice and an opportunity for administrative review in 
accordance with the Corporation’s policies and procedures. No Participating Dentist 
may use any Delta Dental service mark without the Corporation’s permission.
3. Diagnosis and Treatment: Neither this Corporation, nor any member of its Board of 
Directors, its officers, employees, agents, or committees shall impose any restrictions on 
dentists who administer to its subscribers as to methods of diagnosis or treatment. The 
relationship between a subscriber and a dentist treating him/her shall be identical with 
the relationship that ordinarily exists in the community between a dentist and his/her 
patient.
4. Binding Nature of Subscriber Contracts and Dentist Handbook: Every Participating 
Dentist shall be bound by any contract entered into by the Corporation (as approved 
by the Insurance Commissioner of the State of West Virginia) insofar as the contract 
dictates the services to be rendered to subscribers, the fees to be paid therefor, and any 
other matter pertaining to the obligation of the Corporation to the subscriber. Every 
Participating Dentist shall also be bound by the Dentist Handbook issued by and which 
may be revised from time to time by the Corporation.
5. Reports: Participating Dentists shall furnish to the Corporation all reports required 
by action of the Board of Directors or by any officer or other representative of the 
Corporation acting under the authority of the Board of Directors.Bylaws of Delta Dental Plan of West Virginia, Inc. (continued)

APPENDIX B - Mid-Atlantic Bylaws6. Usual Customary and Reasonable Fee Change to Maximum Plan Allowance: Any 
references to Usual Customary and Reasonable Fee (UCR) in Participating Dentist 
Agreements shall be changed to Maximum Plan Allowance (MPA) and Allowed Amount 
as those terms are substituted for UCR in dental service contracts, in regulating the 
services to be rendered to subscribers, the fees to be paid therefor, and any other 
matter pertaining to the obligation of the Corporation to a subscriber.
7. Professional Liability Insurance: All Participating Dentists shall be required to 
carry professional liability insurance with minimum coverage limitations of at least 
$500,000/$1 million which level shall be reviewed from time to time by the Corporation 
for reasonableness and accessibility.
8. Privacy, Accuracy and Availability of Subscriber Records: Every Participating Dentist 
shall safeguard subscriber privacy and confidentiality, consistent with all federal and 
state laws, and ensure the accuracy of subscriber dental information and records 
and enrollment information as conveyed by the Corporation. A Participating Dentist 
shall produce patient records containing health information for the Corporation when 
requested without undue delay for use in the Corporation’s claims administration/
payment activities as authorized by HIPAA under 45 C.F.R. §164.506.
9. Compliance with Applicable Regulatory Requirements. Each Participating Dentist 
shall comply with all laws, regulations and rules applicable to those dental programs 
offered by the Corporation in which the Participating Dentist participates, including but 
not limited to requirements regarding records retention and audits and inspections by 
relevant governmental agencies.
10. Certification with Regard to Governmental Programs. All PPO Participating Dentists 
who treat subscribers in the Corporation’s dental programs which are subject to 
specific state or federal regulation certify that they are not excluded or suspended from 
participation in any federal healthcare program, that they will check the appropriate 
databases at least annually to determine whether they or an affiliated party has been 
suspended or excluded from participation in the Medicare program or any other federal 
healthcare program and that if so, they shall be removed from any work directly or 
indirectly related to all federal healthcare programs pursuant to 45 C.F.R. Part 76, which 
concerns the government-wide system of debarment and suspension.
11. Application of Community Standards to all Services Provided to Subscribers. No 
Participating Dentist shall charge for services to a subscriber, whether or not such 
services are covered as a benefit under contracts entered into by the Corporation, 
unless and until such services meet community standards of generally accepted dental 
practice.
12. Amendments. Participating Dentist agrees to be bound by amendments to the 
Participating Dentist Agreement with advance written notice from Corporation, as 
required by state or federal law. If Participating Dentist does not wish to be bound 
by such amendment, Participating Dentist shall notify Corporation of his/her intent 
to terminate the Agreement within the notice period. Participating Dentist shall 
comply with any amendment required by law until the effective date of termination. 
The foregoing notice requirements shall not apply to amendments agreed to by 
mutual written consent of the parties or to amendments required for compliance with 
applicable law and regulations.Bylaws of Delta Dental Plan of West Virginia, Inc. (continued)

APPENDIX B - Mid-Atlantic Bylaws13. Notices. Any notice required under the Participating Dentist Agreement shall be sent 
to a party’s mailing address of record by United States first-class mail or by overnight 
delivery. Any notice sent by first-class mail shall be deemed to have been received by 
the addressee seventy-two (72) hours after the notice has been deposited in the U.S.

ARTICLE NINE
NOTICES
Any notice provided for in these Bylaws shall be sufficient if mailed, by United States 
mail, or sent by electronic transmission, to the person whom it is directed within the 
time herein prescribed for sending such notice. The certificate of the person or party 
sending the notice setting forth the fact of such mailing or electronic transmission and 
specifying the date thereof shall be sufficient proof of notice. Any notice requirement, 
including the timing of the notice, may be waived by writing signed by the person to 
whom the notice is directed.
ARTICLE TEN
AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS AND ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION
These Bylaws, except for Articles Two and Ten, may be amended at any meeting of the 
directors by the affirmative vote of at least two thirds of all the directors present and 
voting, provided a quorum is present and that notice of the proposed amendments has 
been given to all the directors at least fifteen (15) days before the meeting, by United 
States mail or electronic transmission. Notice of such meeting may be waived by written 
waiver signed by all directors. Articles Two and Ten and the Articles of Incorporation of 
the Corporation shall only be amended at an annual or special meeting of the members 
held for that purpose by a three-fourths vote of all the members present and voting, 
provided a quorum is present and that notice of the proposed amendments has been 
given to all the members at least fifteen (15) days before the meeting.Bylaws of Delta Dental Plan of West Virginia, Inc. (continued)

I. About this user guide
  Welcome to your Online Provider Tools User Guide! This guide contains all the essential information you need to 
make full use of your online account at deltadentalins.com .
   We have included a description of each tool’s functions and capabilities, as well as instructions for common actions 
that will help streamline your daily interactions with us.
  If your patient does not know which Delta Dental company administers his or her plan, you should start with the 
National Search option. This will allow you to quickly identify the Delta Dental company you would submit your claim 
to. There are 39 Delta Dental companies working together to create smiles, improve health, and enhance lives.
 • Delta Dental of California
 • Delta Dental of Pennsylvania (PA and MD)
 • Delta Dental of West Virginia, Inc.
 • Delta Dental of Delaware, Inc.
  After logging into your account, you will see the Provider Tools  landing page. It has all the tools you need to take 
care of business, all in one convenient place.

 Log in to your account at deltadentalins.com .

III. Your Provider Tools landing page
 After successfully logging in to your account, you will arrive at the Provider Tools  landing page.
  The Provider Tools applications that display are based on your participation/contract status and the state in which 
you practice. 
  The dentist name and practice location address will always display at the top right of every page. For practices with 
multiple locations, you can change the location by clicking on Switch office .
 
 TIP:   If the information displayed for your practice location does not appear to be accurate, please use an update 
form (found in the right-most column at deltadentalins.com/dentists ) to advise us. Most update requests require 
approximately two to three weeks processing time.
IV. My patients
  This is a comprehensive list of your Delta Dental patients for whom you’ve submitted claims during the past several 
years. This list will continue to expand as you submit claims for additional patients who are active in our database. 
You can also manually add patients after verifying their eligibility and benefits information. Your My patients  page  is 
updated nightly from the previous day’s claims.
 TIP:  You can easily search for a patient on your list by typing the name in the Find patient  search box. A list of your 
existing patients will start appearing below the box. You can select a patient at any time from that list by clicking 
on their name.
  This tool provides a snapshot of each patient’s name, date of birth, ID number, plan type, eligibility status, remaining 
maximums and remaining deductibles.
 
      
 
 TIP:  The remaining maximum and deductible expand and  
collapse to show a summary of remaining amounts when  
you click on these arrows.

  You can create a work list of the Delta Dental patients you will see each day (i.e., a subset of your entire My patients  
list). From this list, it’s easy to look up eligibility and benefits in preparation for the patients’ visits.
 To create a work list:
 1. Search for a patient.
 2. Check the box next to their name.
 3. Click Add to my work list .
 A message will display that the patient(s) has/have been successfully added.
 
  At any time, you can click on View my work list  to look at only the patients you have added.  
In the screenshot below the user added a total of four patients.

 To view/print a summary of eligibility and benefits for the selected patients on your work list:
 1. Check the box next to the patient’s name.

 To remove a patient or several patients from your work list:
 1. Check the box next to the patient’s name.
 2. Click Remove selected .
 3. Click on the My patient  link to go back to your regular My Patients  page.
